narrative.overview:
The site is not a page about a terminal; it is a plane of instrument surfaces with a morning of research laid across it. The ground is a fixed ruled graticule — four repeating-gradient layers under a radial mask — so the whole document reads as something measured rather than something composed. Content sits on that ground in seamed regions divided by hairline borders, never in floating cards. A fixed time rail on the left carries the session's timestamps like the scale on an instrument; it activates only while the session is in view, because a rail that tracked the whole document would be a minimap, and a minimap is decoration.

The palette, the two typefaces and the semantic colors are inherited wholesale from Gamma's implemented application tokens. Nothing here is a marketing-only color. The one structural inversion is typographic: the application defaults to mono and opts into sans for chrome, while the site defaults to the display sans and opts a named list of data classes into mono — the same Two-Type Rule, entered from the other side, because the site carries prose the app does not.

Restraint is enforced by role, not by taste. Chrome is grey on grey; hue appears only where a value has direction or a state has a name. The only two shadows in the system sit under the two objects that depict a screen. The refusal the product is built on — Gamma cannot place an order — is given a full seamed region with semantic checkmarks and crosses rather than a footnote, and every sample value on the page wears a MOCK badge, because a marketing surface that quietly showed synthetic numbers as live would contradict the product it is selling.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled graticule ground, fixed behind everything, masked to fade downward
One accent (#7aa6c8), used for state and action only; data supplies the rest of the color
Hairline seams (1px) instead of gaps, cards, or radii above 4px
Instrument caps: 10–11px uppercase labels at 0.10–0.16em tracking name every region
Every number, ticker, timestamp, path and stamped label is monospace
Sample data is always badged; planned things are always dashed
Motion is functional — a pour-in on entry, a sweep that tracks reading position, one board that ticks
Nothing is hidden by an overflow-x mask; wide content scrolls inside its own container

rules.name: The Data-Owns-Color Rule
rules.body: Chrome is grey. Hue enters only where a value has a direction (positive/negative), a state has a name (live/mock/planned), or an action is primary. A section heading, a nav item at rest, a card border, and a body paragraph are never colored.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: #7aa6c8 is the only chrome accent on the site. #c49a5a is analytical — warnings, environment values, sample-data badges — and never a second brand color. If a new element wants a third color, it wants a semantic role that already exists.

rules.name: The Labeled-Absence Rule
rules.body: Anything sample, planned, or degraded says so in color and in shape: sample data wears a brass Mock badge, planned things wear a dashed grey badge-plan, and a degradation note carries a brass left rule. No synthetic value on this site is ever presented unbadged.

rules.name: The Two-Type Rule
rules.body: Sans explains the instrument; mono carries the research. Inherited verbatim from docs/design_principles.md, but implemented from the opposite default: body is Archivo, and mono is opt-in via one named selector list in the stylesheet. Adding a data element means adding its class to that list, not setting font-family locally. Never set sans on a number; never force navigation into mono because the product is terminal-like.

rules.name: The Instrument-Caps Rule
rules.body: Every structural label is 10–11px, weight 600, uppercase, tracked 0.10–0.16em, in --text-3. A label names a container that is present; it is never a floating eyebrow above a headline, and it never carries a sentence.

rules.name: The Tracking-Inversion Rule
rules.body: Tracking runs negative as type grows and positive as it shrinks: -0.042em at display, -0.028em at headline, -0.02em at title, normal at body, +0.08em to +0.16em at label. A 10px cap set at normal tracking is a bug.

rules.name: The Fluid-Minimum Rule
rules.body: Every auto-placed grid track is written minmax(min(Npx, 100%), 1fr). The min() guarantees the declared minimum never exceeds the viewport, so no grid can push the page wider than the screen at any width.

rules.name: The No-Mask Rule
rules.body: There is no overflow-x: hidden anywhere in the system. Wide content is given its own scroll container instead — the table wrapper, the code block's pre, the live board's tab strip, the nav strip below 860px, and the screenshot frame below 760px. Hiding overflow hides a layout bug; scrolling it admits one honestly.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by 1px borders, not by gaps or drop shadows. Region seams use --panel-border; divisions inside a region use the fainter --rule or a ~14% alpha hairline. A gap where a seam belongs makes the plane read as loose cards.

rules.name: The Flat-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Only an object that depicts a screen may cast a shadow. Everything else conveys depth with a tonal step and a hairline. A shadow on a button, a badge, a card, or a table is out of system.

rules.name: The Visible-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: .reveal resolves to opacity: 1. The pour-in — a 620ms rise from 15px with a 3px blur clearing — is applied by adding a class on intersection, and only inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block on a .js root. A failed observer, a disabled script, or a reduced-motion preference costs the animation and never the copy.

dos: Do inherit the palette from Gamma's application tokens. This site has no marketing-only color, and adding one would break the claim that the screenshots and the page are the same world.
Do add a new data element's class to the mono selector list in site.css rather than setting font-family on it locally. That list is the Two-Type Rule's only implementation.
Do name every region with instrument caps (10–11px, 600, uppercase, 0.10–0.16em) in --text-3.
Do separate regions with a 1px --panel-border seam and divide inside them with the fainter --rule.
Do write auto-placed grid tracks as minmax(min(Npx, 100%), 1fr).
Do give wide content its own scroll container, and label it when the gesture is not obvious (the screenshot frame's "drag to pan" below 760px).
Do badge every synthetic value Mock and every uncontracted provider badge-plan with its dashed border, on this site as in the app.
Do annotate a screenshot with a numbered .mark-pt plus a legend row, and keep the marker pointer-events: none.
Do keep .reveal's resting state visible and animate only on entry.
Do state a limit plainly and give it weight — the boundary region is a full seamed field, not a disclaimer.
donts: Don't put a shadow on chrome. Only the live board and the screenshot plate cast one; everything else uses a tonal step and a hairline.
Don't introduce a radius above 4px, or use a circle for anything that is not a status dot or a numbered marker.
Don't color chrome. A heading, a nav item at rest, a card border, or a body paragraph is grey; hue belongs to values, states, and the one primary action.
Don't treat brass (#c49a5a) as a second brand accent. It is the analytical / warning role: env strings, code values, mock badges, degradation rules.
Don't add overflow-x: hidden anywhere. If something overflows, either fix the track minimum or give it a scroll container.
Don't float a callout over a screenshot. The marker points; the legend explains.
Don't set a 10px uppercase label at normal tracking, or set display type without negative tracking.
Don't let the time rail track the whole document or appear below 1180px — it belongs to the session section and needs its own 92px column.
Don't hide content behind a scroll-triggered animation. If the observer never fires, the page must still read completely.
Don't show a number on this site that a real Gamma surface could not produce, and never show one without its provenance or its Mock badge.
